notes: y is the year the state's bias-crime provision was first enacted per MAP's citations or the statute's own history; MAP's table column 'Year Hate Crime Law Passed' mostly dates sexual-orientation/gender-identity additions, so it was not used. null = not established from sources read.

Statute text not reached for KY, MS, NH, NJ, NM (support from Lawyers' Committee FAQ 2018 and MAP only) and AL (Legislature bill synopses 2010/2013 plus FAQ). WI read via FindLaw mirror; CA, CO, NY, TX via Public.Law mirrors; IL via ilga.gov through a fetch tool; CT text is the 2021 DCJ compilation.

Connecticut P.A. 26-77 (SB 90, signed 5/26/2026) revised and consolidated the hate-crime statutes; the new text was not reviewed, and status stays enacted based on the prior statute and the Act's title.

Arkansas and Indiana are partial: Ark. Code 5-4-405 (Act 681 of 2021) and IC 35-38-1-7.1(a)(12) (2019) address victim-group or bias selection without naming race, ethnicity or national origin. MAP and Brennan do not count either as a hate-crime law; ADL and others may differ.

North Dakota (civil-rights-style offense limited to use of public facilities) and Ohio (ethnic intimidation limited to menacing, property-damage and harassment offenses) are partial under the 'choose the lower status' rule; some trackers count both as having hate-crime laws.
Enacted entries that are sentencing factors or enhancements rather than stand-alone offenses include AK, AZ, KS, KY, MS, NM, TN, TX, ME and WI; Alaska's list says 'creed' rather than 'religion'.

South Carolina: H.3039/S.247 (Pinckney Hate Crimes Act) were not enacted; a May 13, 2026 report said the session ended May 14 with the bill expected to stall. Marked none rather than pending because no evidence shows the bill alive after adjournment; final action not independently confirmed.
Wyoming: no hate-crime statute per MAP and WACH (May 2026); a title search of all 2025 and 2026 bills in the Legislature's data found no hate or bias bill, so none rather than pending.

The web-search budget ran out before sweeps for 2025-26 bills that would amend existing statutes; amending bills are mentioned only where seen (North Carolina H961, 2025). Mississippi bills to expand categories (e.g., HB 364 of 2024, died in committee) were not tracked for 2026.
Data-collection remarks in x come from MAP's citations document and describe whether a state mandates collection; they do not state whether reports go to the FBI except for New Mexico.
